## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #14050 worktree pre-warming — ALREADY IMPLEMENTED (LOW priority, duplicate)

- **What**: Kilocode #14050 "feat(agent-manager): pre-warm worktrees to speed up session creation" optimizes Agent Manager session creation latency by maintaining a pool of pre-created worktrees in the VS Code extension. Alexi already has complete worktree infrastructure: (1) `src/utils/gitWorktree.ts` (95 lines) with `createWorktree` (detached-HEAD worktree at `~/.alexi/worktrees/<uuid>/<repoName>/`), `cleanupWorktree` (removes worktree + empty parent dirs), and `getWorktreeBaseDir` (`~/.alexi/worktrees/`), (2) Integration into agent/task tools (`src/tool/tools/agent-manager.ts`, `src/tool/tools/task.ts`). Pre-warming is a VS Code UI latency optimization (pool of ready worktrees so users see instant session start) that does not apply to CLI architecture where worktrees are created on-demand per agent/task invocation and destroyed after completion. No feature gap.
- **Why**: The feature Kilocode added (worktree pooling, pre-creation) is specific to long-running GUI application lifecycle optimization. CLI tools create worktrees on-demand (milliseconds overhead acceptable for multi-second LLM calls). Adding pre-warming to Alexi CLI would waste disk space (pooled worktrees unused between invocations) and add complexity (lifecycle management, cleanup across CLI runs) with no user benefit. The foundational worktree infrastructure Alexi needs is already complete.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14050 (Kilocode worktree pre-warming), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/utils/gitWorktree.ts (Alexi worktree implementation)
- **Category**: tool (git, worktree, agent isolation) — DUPLICATE / NOT APPLICABLE
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Foundational feature already done; pre-warming optimization not applicable to CLI.

These are GUI interaction features: keyboard navigation, dropdown rendering, insertion, and cleanup of the mention UI widget. Not applicable to CLI text-based input. Alexi already has inline model override (`@provider/model` pattern in `src/core/inlineModelOverride.ts`, 64 lines, ported from Kilocode #14006, issue #1716 resolved) which is the CLI-portable version of @ mentions for model selection.

The @ mention pattern Alexi CLI needs (model override) already exists. No additional @ mention features from Kilocode are portable.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14106 (@ mention menu close fix), https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14111 (UI refactoring), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/inlineModelOverride.ts (Alexi inline model override implementation)

#### 5. Cline #12267 Crusoe provider — NOT APPLICABLE (LOW priority, architecture mismatch)

- **What**: Cline #12267 "feat: add Crusoe as an OpenAI-compatible provider" adds Crusoe Cloud as an OpenAI-compatible provider (API endpoint + key). Crusoe is a GPU cloud provider offering OpenAI API compatibility for models like Llama, Mistral. Cline's provider architecture supports arbitrary OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Alexi's provider architecture is fundamentally different: all models are deployed in SAP AI Core and accessed via SAP Orchestration API (`src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts`), model catalog is dynamically fetched from SAP AI Core deployments (`src/providers/modelCatalog.ts`), and routing is SAP-deployment-aware. Adding external providers (Crusoe, OpenRouter, etc.) would require architectural redesign (new provider abstraction, multi-backend routing, credential management for non-SAP services) that is out of scope for single-feature recommendations.
- **Why**: Alexi is purpose-built for SAP AI Core. External provider support is a strategic product decision, not a tactical feature addition. Not actionable for research brief.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/12267 (Crusoe provider)
- **Category**: provider (external, OpenAI-compatible) — NOT APPLICABLE
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Architecture mismatch.

#### 6. Aider #5173 Claude model name expansion — NOT NEEDED (LOW priority, auto-discovery)

- **What**: Aider #5173 "Expand ANTHROPIC_MODELS list with recent Claude model names" adds missing Claude model names (`claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219`, `claude-opus-4-1`, `claude-opus-4-5`, `claude-opus-4-6-20260205`, `claude-opus-4-7-20260416`) to Aider's `ANTHROPIC_MODELS` static list in `aider/models.py`. Aider uses this list to map bare model names (no provider prefix) to the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable for `sanity_check_models`. Alexi's model catalog (`src/providers/modelCatalog.ts`) uses a fundamentally different approach: (1) Dynamic deployment fetching from SAP AI Core at startup (`refreshModelCatalog()`, lines 98-342), (2) Provider prefix patterns (`anthropic--`, `gpt-`, `gemini-`, `deepseek-`, etc., line 39-48) to identify LLM deployments, (3) Static fallback list (`ORCHESTRATION_MODELS` from `src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts`) when API unreachable, (4) Automatic discovery: any Claude model deployed in SAP AI Core with `configurationName` starting with `anthropic--` is automatically added to the catalog. Manual expansion of Claude model names is not needed — SAP AI Core is the source of truth.
- **Why**: Alexi's architecture auto-discovers available models from SAP AI Core. When a new Claude model (e.g. Opus 4.7) is deployed to SAP AI Core, it appears in the catalog automatically on next refresh (5min TTL). No code changes needed. Aider's static list maintenance pattern does not apply.
- **Source**: https://github.com/aider-ai/aider/pull/5173 (Aider model list expansion), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/modelCatalog.ts (Alexi dynamic catalog)
- **Category**: provider (model catalog, Claude models) — NOT NEEDED
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Auto-discovery architecture makes manual expansion unnecessary.

#### 7. Aider #5132 bash tree-sitter tags — ALREADY IMPLEMENTED (LOW priority, duplicate)

- **What**: Aider #5132 "feat: add bash tree-sitter tags for repomap support" adds bash function extraction to Aider's repomap (code context / symbol index) using tree-sitter-bash grammar. Extracts top-level bash functions (`name() { ... }` and `function name [()] { ... }` syntaxes) so the repomap can show bash script structure. Alexi already has complete bash tree-sitter support: (1) `src/context/treeSitter.ts` declares `tree-sitter-bash` as optional peer dependency (lines 50, 60, 80), lazy-loads the grammar on first parse, and provides `getBashParser()` (lines 10-93 of grep output), (2) `src/context/symbols.ts` extracts bash symbols (lines 118-182): `isBashFile()` detects `.sh`/`.bash` extensions, `extractBashSymbols()` extracts top-level `function_definition` nodes, `extractBashSignature()` builds compact signatures (`name()` or `function name`), handles both POSIX-style and Bash keyword-style function declarations, (3) Repomap integration (`src/context/repoMap.ts` line 1 comment: "extracts symbols via tree-sitter, ranks files by import importance"), (4) Tests in `src/context/__tests__/symbols.test.ts` (line 5 comment: "Symbol extraction depends on tree-sitter grammars (optional peer deps)"). No gaps.
- **Why**: The feature Aider added (bash function extraction for repomap) already exists in Alexi with identical semantics (tree-sitter-bash grammar, function name extraction, signature formatting, top-level filtering). No work needed.
- **Source**: https://github.com/aider-ai/aider/pull/5132 (Aider bash tree-sitter tags), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/context/treeSitter.ts (grammar loading), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/context/symbols.ts lines 118-182 (bash symbol extraction), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/package.json (tree-sitter-bash peer dependency)
- **Category**: tool (repomap, tree-sitter, code indexing, bash) — DUPLICATE
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Already done.
